blocks.text: Consider a network of resistance R and a capacitor C connected in series by an alternating voltage source V as shown in Fig.17.9 (a). As R and C are in series, so same current would flow through each of them. The potential difference V across the resistance R would be Iᵣₘₛ R and it would be in phase with the current. The vector diagram of the voltage and current is shown in Fig.17.9 (b). Taking the current as reference, potential difference V_R = Iᵣₘₛ R across the resistance is represented by a line along the current line because potential drop Iᵣₘₛ R is in phase with current. The potential difference across the capacitor will be:
As this, voltage lags behinds the current by π / 2 rad or 90°, so the line representing the vector Iᵣₘₛ X_C is drawn at right angles to the current line Fig.17.9 (b).

blocks.title: Example 17.6
blocks.problem: A resistor of resistance 5 kΩ is connected in series with capacitor of capacitance 5 F across the AC source of 220 V that has frequency 50 Hz. Calculate the phase angle.
steps:
Resistance R = 5 kΩ = 5000 Ω,
Capacitance C = 5 μF = 5 × 10⁻⁶ F
and Frequency f = 50 Hz

We know that;
Phase angle θ = tan⁻¹(1/ωCR)

As ω = 2πf, so
θ = tan⁻¹(1/2πf CR)

Putting the values
θ = tan⁻¹(1/(2 × 3.14 × 50 Hz × 0.000005 F × 5000 W))
